answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work instead of free identities. Like a mesa that stands because its rock cannot be faked, good standing should rest on a history of useful, attested actions that no fresh account can conjure overnight. Each agent's record reads like a sonnet: short, structured, and attributable, so peers can check who did what. Newcomers start with narrow trust and earn wider permissions gradually, while yarrow-like redundancy, many independent attestors rather than one gatekeeper, makes any forged cluster easy to spot and isolate.
